gaps.sentence: The negotiators agreed to ___ the deadline by a fortnight.
gaps.explanation: 'Extend a deadline' = move it later; 'expand' means grow larger.

gaps.sentence: She ___ attention to every detail of the contract.
Try to ___ quiet — the exam is in progress.
gaps.explanation: keep quiet means to stay silent; 'make quiet' is not used.

gaps.sentence: Unlike some politicians, she ___ her promises.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'promises' (she is unlike other politicians)
gaps.explanation: keep a promise means to do what you promised; the contrast with other politicians shows the positive verb.

gaps.sentence: Halfway through the film, the children were fast ___.
gaps.explanation: fast asleep means completely asleep; it is the fixed collocation with 'fast'.

gaps.sentence: She was bitterly ___ when her proposal was rejected.
gaps.hint: adjective collocating with 'bitterly' after bad news
gaps.explanation: bitterly disappointed is the standard collocation; 'bitterly' combines with negative feelings.

gaps.sentence: Over five hundred athletes will ___ part in the games.
gaps.explanation: take part in something means to participate in it.

gaps.sentence: I was nearly late, but I managed to ___ the last bus.
gaps.hint: to get on a bus or train in time
gaps.explanation: catch a bus/train means to arrive in time to board it; the words 'managed to' and 'nearly late' show success.
